known_gaps: turning the customer's words into negotiation events (and dates into YYYY-MM-DD) is done by the dialogue model; offers, counters, dates, amounts, read-back, recording, notes and the close are code
callback window validity is decided by the dialogue model from code-computed window facts (not code)
identity flow (which question, re-asks, declines) follows the dialogue model with the bank's verification results

extra rule (stateful, stage opening): Confirmation that the right person is on the line: ask at most twice, answer the customer's questions first, then close not_reached/unclear. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage identity): Count wrong answers across both questions. Three in total close the call as not_verified/failed and point the customer to the mobile app or a branch. A day_month_swapped retry does not count. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage identity): Declining identity: explain once that the questions protect the account. A second refusal, or a second question about what the call is about, closes not_verified/declined. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Count persuasion attempts by band: early 1, late 2. Each flat refusal, non-answer, refused floor, refused below-floor substitute or refused deadline uses one. When none are left, close no_promise/refused without repeating a refused offer. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Offer the floor only once after 'too much', and say the rest stays overdue. The only exception is attempt 2 (floor on the deadline). - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): Interpret 'next <weekday>' as that weekday in the following calendar week and 'this <weekday>' as the one in the current week, relative to now. Then validate the date in code. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Hardship (illness, death in the family, job loss): one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion, offer support. Accept: transfer to support. Decline: no_promise/hardship. This takes precedence over rules 30 and 41. A date or amount the customer names themselves is still handled under sections 7 and 8. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): A change to the date or amount at confirmation invalidates the earlier confirmation. Re-check the new value and read it back again before create_promise. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage global): A human request: ask once whether you can help first. Transfer to the general queue only if the customer insists. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage global): If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk: no_promise/refused after verification, not_verified/declined before it. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage closing): If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as transferred with that transfer's reason, not as promise. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
